answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the wharf schedule in the gale ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the whisper checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 58 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 33 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
